bibliographic.title: The ChatGPT (Generative Artificial Intelligence) Revolution Has Made Artificial Intelligence Approachable for Medical Professionals
bibliographic.citation_apa: Mesko, B. (2023). The ChatGPT (Generative Artificial Intelligence) Revolution Has Made Artificial Intelligence Approachable for Medical Professionals. Journal of Medical Internet Research, 25, e48392. https://doi.org/10.2196/48392

methodology.technology_context: ChatGPT, GPT-4, large language models, generative artificial intelligence, conversational agents, chatbots in medical practice and education

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article is a JMIR Viewpoint centered on how public access to ChatGPT and LLMs changed physician attitudes and accelerated generative AI products in health care. It names LLMs, chatbots, and conversational agents and briefly notes ethics-related risks, but the provided text contains no systematic treatment of conversational governance, guardrails, audit, observability, human oversight, or compliance mechanisms required for central evidence in this review.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Python borderline score (77.33, grade B) with strong LLM and healthcare signals but weak governance signals; only page 1/front matter provided, so governance coverage beyond ethics mentions cannot be fully verified.

appraisal.notes: Viewpoint article with a clear argumentative objective but no empirical design, sample, or transparent data-collection protocol. Ethics risks are acknowledged via citations, but governance mechanisms are not analyzed. Limitations of the viewpoint itself are not evident in the provided excerpt.

cerqual.explanation: The argument is internally coherent as commentary on ChatGPT-driven adoption in medicine, but the provided evidence is thin for governance claims and offers no operational or empirical support for conversational governance in regulated settings.

coding.theme: Adoption of LLMs and generative AI in health care
coding.subtheme: ChatGPT as catalyst for physician engagement with AI
rq_alignment: partial alignment via ethics and risk mentions only

synthesis.main_claim: Public attention, access, and debate around LLMs, especially ChatGPT, initiated a wave of generative AI products and services in health care and may change physicians' perceptions of AI.
synthesis.contribution: Provides contextual commentary on post-November 2022 LLM diffusion, healthcare use-case examples, and brief acknowledgment of ethics-related challenges such as hallucination, authorship debate, cybersecurity, and bias.
synthesis.limitations: Non-empirical viewpoint; no systematic review method; governance, oversight, audit, and operational controls are not developed in the provided text.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as foundational contextual evidence for the timing and scale of ChatGPT/LLM adoption in health care and for high-level awareness of ethics risks, not as central evidence on conversational governance.
